narrative.overview: The product looks like the paper a halal butcher wraps food in: a warm cream ground, kraft-toned rules, ink-dark type, and a red brand stamp pressed onto it. Trust is not a green dot — it is a seal, rendered as a literal stamp with a dashed edge, because the product's promise is that a human reviewed a certificate. Nothing is clinical, nothing glows, nothing floats. The system is deliberately physical. Corners are nearly square (4–10px), shadows are hard offset blocks of ink rather than soft blur, and pressing a control translates it into its own shadow. Type does the hierarchy work: Archivo carries voice (wordmark, headings, labels, buttons), Space Grotesk carries reading (body, meta, numerals).
keyCharacteristics: Cream paper ground (#fbf7ee) everywhere, kraft-rule borders, ink type.
Butcher red for actions and the wordmark apostrophe; stamp green only for verification.
Verification drawn as a seal: dashed stamp-200 edge, stamp-50 fill, stamp-700 mark.
Hard offset shadows; press-down interaction; no soft blur, no glass, no gradients.
Colorblind-safe by construction: every status pairs a distinct glyph family with a word.

rules.name: The Two Reds Rule
rules.body: Brand red and danger red never share a component. Errors are recognized by the alert triangle plus wording, not by hue.

rules.name: The Green Means Reviewed Rule
rules.body: Stamp green is reserved for a certificate a committee actually reviewed. Form success is neutral ink confirmation; a lapse is informational, never green and never red.

rules.name: The Two-Face Rule
rules.body: Archivo never sets a paragraph and Space Grotesk never sets a button.

rules.name: The One Ground Rule
rules.body: No page introduces a second background color. Banding, if used, is cream-tinted; panels sit on it as paper-white sheets.

rules.name: The Press-Down Rule
rules.body: Every pressable control translates by its own shadow offset and collapses the shadow; reduced motion keeps the shadow change only.

rules.name: The No-Soft-Corner Rule
rules.body: If a surface needs to feel soft, it is wrong for this world — tighten the radius.

dos: Do use tokens for every color, radius and shadow; a hardcoded hex is a bug.
Do pair every status color with a glyph family and a word.
Do keep Verified and Unverified metrics identical so grids do not shift.
Do keep interactive targets at least 44×44px, including icon-only controls.
Do reserve the dashed border for seals, dividers and empty panels.
donts: Don't use stamp green for generic success, or danger red for Unverified.
Don't put brand red and danger red in the same component.
Don't soften to large radii, blurred shadows, glass panels, or gradient text.
Don't introduce a second page background or a second accent.
Don't add a border-left/right accent stripe on alerts or cards.
Don't invent imagery, testimonials, ratings or certifiers that are not in data.
